Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 86, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat al-Tariq

It is Meccan.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the sky and the one who comes at night﴾. Al-Tariq here is the star. As for in the language of the Arabs, al-Tariq is everything that knocks (yatruqu) at night. It has also been said: it is the one that knocks at night or by day.

As for the saying of the poet:

(We are the daughters of al-Tariq...)

That is: the daughters of the stars, in nobility and loftiness.

And Jarir said:

(The one who visits you at night, the captivator of hearts, and this is not the time for lingering, so return in peace.)

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the night-comer is?﴾ He said this because the word *al-tariq* (the night-comer) applies to the star and to other things. So He mentioned here His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the night-comer is?﴾, because the Messenger did not know which night-comer was meant.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 86, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿The piercing star﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: the bright one (al-Mudi').

And on the authority of Mujahid: it is the one that blazes (al-Mutawahhij).

And on the authority of some of them: it is the one that is revolving (al-Mustadir).

And on the authority of some of them: "the piercing star" is the star that pierces the devils with fire.

Al-Farra' mentioned that it is Saturn (Zuhal), and it is the largest of the stars.

This opinion has also been related on the authority of 'Ali.

And on the authority of some of them: it is a star which Allah created in the seventh heaven, and He created nothing else in it, which knocks upon (yatriqu) the heavens and then returns to its place.

According to the opinion we have mentioned [that Saturn is the piercing one], meaning that it pierces the heavens with its light.

And on the authority of Ibn Zayd: it is the Pleiades (al-Thurayya).

When the Arabs use the word "the star" (al-najm) without qualification, they mean by it the Pleiades (al-Thurayya).

Its saying, ﴿Indeed, every soul has over it a guardian﴾, is the response to the oath.

It has been read with both shaddah and without shaddah. The meaning with shaddah is: "No soul but has over it a guardian" (illa ʿalayha ḥafiẓ), and the meaning without shaddah is: "Perhaps it has a guardian" (laʿallaha ḥafiẓ), and "mā" is extra (zāʾidah). The guardian is the angel (al-malak). It is also reported from some of them: his companion who guards his deeds upon him. It was said: the guardian is Allah, Exalted is He, who guards their deeds upon them.

Translation:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾, meaning: from what thing he was created.

"And His saying: ﴿Created from a gushing fluid﴾, meaning: poured forth (mدفوق), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿In a pleasant life﴾, meaning: pleasing (مرضية). And it is said: ﴿gushing fluid﴾ means: flowing, pouring out continuously."

And His saying: ﴿It issues from between the loins and the ribs﴾, i.e., from the loins of the man and the ribs (tara'ib) of the woman.

It is related in a report that it issues from every vertebra of his loins. The tara'ib are eight ribs: four on the right side and four on the left. It is also said that they are the chest; it is also said that they are between the two breasts; and it is also said that they are what lies below the collarbone.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 86, verse 8:

Concerning His words, ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him,﴾ there are several opinions. The first: He is able to return the drop of semen into the urethra, said by Mujahid, Ibrahim and Ikrimah. The second opinion: He is able to return him to the state of childhood. It has also been said: He returns him from old age (al-shaykhukha) to middle age (al-kuhula), from middle age to youth, from youth to childhood, from childhood to infancy, from infancy to the womb of the mother, and from the womb to the loins (al-sulb). This is the meaning of His words, ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him.﴾

The third opinion, which is the best of the opinions, is that what is meant is that He is able to bring him back to life after death. This was mentioned by al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and others.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day when hidden things are tested﴾. That is, they are examined and tested. It is said: they are made manifest, and this is the preferable view.

In the tafsir it is related that every person's secret is revealed, and its effect appears upon his face, so some faces become white and some faces become black.

And His saying: ﴿Then he will have no power, nor any helper﴾ — meaning: no power by which he may strengthen himself, and no helper to aid him, so that through them he might repel the punishment from himself.

Concerning the Almighty's words, ﴿By the sky, which has the return﴾, that is: the rain. This is the well-known view, and rain is called "return" (raj') because it returns again and again.

The second view: it refers to the sun, the moon and the stars. They are called "return" because they rise and set, and they return from the west to the east.
And His saying: ﴿And the earth that splits open﴾ means: the vegetation. This is the view of all of them. It is called "splitting" (ṣad') because the earth splits open by means of it.
Its saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾ means: possessing decisiveness, which is the distinguishing between truth and falsehood.
And His saying: ﴿And it is not a jest﴾, i.e., it is not play or idle sport. The meaning is that it is a word of earnestness.

Divine saying, "Indeed, they are plotting a plot" (Qur'an 86:15): meaning, they are scheming a scheme. In the language, kayd (plotting, guile) is an action by which one reaches a goal in secrecy and concealment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 86, verse 16:

﴿And I plan a plan.﴾ The plotting (kayd) from Allah is the gradual leading-on (istidraj) from where they do not know, the disbelievers. Istidraj is seizing [them] little by little. It was said: it is seizing [them] from where it is hidden from them. It was also said: ﴿And I plan a plan.﴾ meaning: I will punish them with a punishment equal to their plotting.

And His saying: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers﴾ means: give respite to the disbelievers. This was before the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf, the verse commanding fighting against the disbelievers).

And His saying: ﴿Give them respite, a little while﴾ means: give them respite for a short time. The Arabs say: رويدك يا فلان, meaning: be at ease (ʾawdah) and gentle (rifq). Here, however, it carries the meaning of "a little," as we have explained.

He had already seized them with the sword on the day of Badr, and He will seize them with the punishment of the Hereafter soon.
